answer: Basalt Ledger Decay. Each identity accrues reputation as a pigment-like score that decays on a spiral schedule: every action an agent takes must reference a recent prior action, and unreferenced scores fall off geometrically. Clones start at zero and must pay full compute price per reference, so a sybil farm burns real resources faster than its scores accumulate. The per-identity cost to an attacker scales superlinearly with clone count because each new identity must independently rebuild its decay chain.
